trust_decision.summary: CorsFilter decides whether a request Origin is trusted (checkOrigin: '*' or set membership) and then echoes that Origin back with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true whenever allowCredentials is set (default true), so a '*' config grants credentialed access to any origin.

landing_point.why: The summary names CorsFilter and the wildcard config; checkOrigin is the only origin check and the '*' test is on that line. The whole mechanism sits in this 177-line file.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver could argue the preflight response (OPTIONS) only advertises permissions and the real exposure is the actual-request response filter, or the other way round. Both sit in the same file, a few lines apart.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: With an explicit allowedOrigins list and allowCredentials=true (the default), the filter must keep echoing the matched origin with Allow-Credentials:true and Vary:Origin. Also, '*' with allowCredentials=false must keep allowing any origin. An over-broad fix that rejects '*' or drops credentials for every origin breaks both.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Origin matching that also accepts a 'null' origin or subdomain/suffix patterns from allowedOrigins, each still echoed with credentials.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Users often ask for wildcard-subdomain origins. A maintainer extending checkOrigin with endsWith-style matching is plausible, and the result would be a parser-differential, how-type sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A transport-specific CORS handler for an embedded adapter (Vert.x/Netty/Undertow) that copies the request Origin into the response headers, as a second implementation at distance.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Embedded adapters sometimes add their own preflight shortcuts outside the JAX-RS filter chain. At the pinned commit none exists (only CorsFilter references CorsHeaders in src/main), so this would be purely planted.
